<color=1.0, 1.0, 0.0>Civilization bonus:</color>
Villagers can hunt and herd livestock.
<color=1.0, 1.0, 0.0>Unique units:</color>
Ashigaru Musketeer, Atakebune, Daimyo, Flaming Arrow, Fune, Sohei Archer, Morutaru, Geomsabok, Tekkousen, Samurai, Gungdo Cavalry, Pyeongon Cavalry, Hongyipao and Yumi Archer.
<color=1.0, 1.0, 0.0>Unique buildings:</color>
Hanok (Korean House), Korean Town Center, Barracks and Stable. Hanoks shelter up to 3 villagers or infantry and, from the Colonial Age, shoot while occupied. Cherry Orchard is a resource for food. Dojo generates armies automatically.
<color=1.0, 1.0, 0.0>Wonders:</color>
Golden Pavilion, Great Buddha, The Shogunate, Torii Gates and Toshogu Shrine

The Joseon dynasty ruled Korea from Hanseong for five centuries and proclaimed the Korean Empire in 1897.
Empress Myeongseong is a shrewd and determined ruler. She seeks strong allies abroad, keeps a watchful eye on every rival and defends her realm with patience before she strikes.

Korean house. Increases the population limit by 10. Up to 3 villagers or infantry can take refuge inside, and the town bell sends villagers in. From the Colonial Age it shoots while occupied: the more units inside, the stronger.
Korean house: population and a refuge for 3 villagers or infantry.

Seungjang (monk general): mounted Buddhist monk and explorer. Builds Town Centers, Trading Posts and Hanoks, shoots with a bow and stuns enemies, and is knocked out instead of killed (ransom him at a Town Center). Monastery techs: Hyangyak Jipseongbang (heal), Dure (nearby villagers gather faster), Pyeonjeon (archery), Seungbyeong (trains warrior monks).
Mounted explorer: builds, shoots and stuns.
Seungjang gain the ability to heal nearby units.
Seungjang bow and stun shot: +4 range and +25% damage.
Villagers near a Seungjang gather 10% faster.
The Seungjang trains Seungbyeong (monk soldiers) in the field, and up to 15 Seungbyeong can serve instead of 10.
Korean monk soldier armed with a glaive. Costs no population (at most 10, 15 with the Seungbyeong monastery tech). Good against cavalry and light infantry.
Monk soldier: no population cost, good against cavalry.
Korean heavy foot soldier armed with a matchlock musket. Good against cavalry in a melee.
Heavy ranged infantry. Good against cavalry and hand infantry.
Jochong Musketeer attack and hitpoints increased.
Korean foot soldier armed with a long spear. Good against cavalry and buildings.
Hand infantry, good against cavalry and buildings
Jangchang Spearman attack and hitpoints increased.
Ranged infantry armed with the Korean horn bow. Good against infantry.
Gakgung Archer attack and hitpoints increased.

Super-heavy artillery. Moves and fires slowly, but does tremendous damage against infantry or buildings.

Bonus: +7% Land Military and Villager Damage

Trains: Yamabushi, Shinobi, Ninja, Ronin

Shipments: Military enhancements, Osaka Ronin
Paper lanterns glowing under the eaves of the city's great halls.
Joseon silk lanterns, red above and blue below for yang and yin, lit for weddings and festive nights.
